create.name: Stephen Jenkinson
create.bio:
Stephen Jenkinson is a Canadian teacher, author and storyteller whose work turns on dying, grief, elderhood and the place of ritual in a culture he sees as having lost its bearings. He studied theology at Harvard and social work in Toronto, earning a master's in each, and as a young man he served an apprenticeship with a master storyteller. For many years he sat with dying people and their families, directed a programme at a large Canadian hospital and taught at a medical school.

In 2010 he and his wife, Nathalie Roy, began the Orphan Wisdom School, which for fourteen years gathered students twice a year in Ontario and also in the Gulf Islands, Wales and Iceland. With the singer-songwriter Gregory Hoskins he created Nights of Grief and Mystery, a touring evening of songs, stories and ceremony that has travelled through North America, Europe and Australasia. His books include Die Wise, on dying well and the culture around it, Come of Age, on what real elderhood asks of us, and Trembling, Still, his most recent. He farms off-grid, builds traditional canoes and sculpts, and he still leads small in-person sessions at the Orphan Wisdom Hall in Ontario, now centred on ritual and ceremony.

books.title: Die Wise: A Manifesto for Sanity and Soul
books.author: Stephen Jenkinson
books.description: His best-known book, drawing on years beside dying people to argue that dying well is a skill and a duty, and that how a culture handles death shapes how it lives.

books.title: Come of Age: The Case for Elderhood in a Time of Trouble
books.author: Stephen Jenkinson
books.description: A reflection on the gap between growing old and becoming an elder, and on what genuine elders could offer a troubled time.

courses.title: The Post, Then the Beam: The 2027 Boreal Session
courses.description: A winter gathering at the Orphan Wisdom Hall exploring ritual as a practice and practice as a ritual, offered as a full week, a weekend, or a weekend livestream.
